content: Tioconazole, commonly marketed under the brand name Vagistat-1, is an antifungal medication specifically used to treat vaginal yeast infections. It is formulated as a 5% ointment for intravaginal application, typically administered as a single dose at bedtime. The medication works by inhibiting the fungal P450 enzyme system, thereby reducing the synthesis of ergosterol, an essential component of fungal cell membranes. This action disrupts the integrity of the fungal cell membrane, leading to the death of the fungal cells. Indications and Usage: Tioconazole is indicated for the treatment of vaginal fungal infections caused by Candida species. It alleviates symptoms such as vaginal burning, itching, and abnormal discharge associated with these infections. However, it is not effective against bacterial or viral infections. Patients experiencing fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, abdominal pain, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge should not use this medication and should consult a healthcare provider, as these symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Administration Instructions: This medication is for vaginal use only. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after application. Avoid contact with the eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse the eyes immediately with plenty of water. To apply, lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest. Insert the applicator filled with the medication into the vagina as far as it comfortably goes. Slowly press the plunger to release the full dose of the ointment. Do not use tampons, douches, spermicides, or other vaginal products while using this medication. If symptoms persist after three days or last more than seven days, consult your doctor. Additionally, if the infection recurs within two months, seek medical advice. Contraindications and Precautions: Tioconazole is contraindicated in individuals with known hypersensitivity to azole antifungals or any inactive ingredients in the formulation. Pregnant women should not use this medication for self-treatment. During pregnancy, it should only be used if clearly needed and under the guidance of a healthcare provider. The safety of tioconazole during lactation is not established, and it is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk. The manufacturer recommends discontinuing breastfeeding while using this medication. This product may weaken latex or rubber products, such as condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to failure. Avoid using these products during treatment and for three days after completing the treatment. Pharmacokinetics: Absorption: Peak plasma concentration of 18 ng/mL is achieved within 2 to 24 hours after application. Onset of Action: Symptom improvement is typically observed within 24 hours, with complete relief occurring within seven days. Metabolism: The drug undergoes glucuronidation of the imidazole ring. Distribution: The medication remains in vaginal fluids for 24 to 72 hours. Excretion: It is eliminated via urine and feces. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, vaginal or urethral burning, itching, or pain. These effects are usually mild and transient. Serious allergic reactions are rare but may include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If any severe reactions occur, seek immediate medical attention. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of tioconazole or increase the risk of adverse effects. Patients should maintain a list of all medications and supplements they are taking and share it with their healthcare provider. This includes prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products. Overdose: If tioconazole is accidentally ingested, it may be harmful. In cases of overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency cases, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S.). Storage and Disposal: Store the medication at room temperature. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Notes for Prevention: To reduce the risk of recurrent vaginal yeast infections, keep the genital area dry after bathing, showering, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight clothing, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp exercise clothes for extended periods. Important Information: This document provides a summary of tioconazole and does not include all possible information about the product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
